statement: codebase/ is a curated, reproducible INPUT SET. The live registry is append-only OPERATIONAL HISTORY. They are different objects and equality between them is not a goal. The condition is CLASSIFICATION, not count: every live name must belong to exactly one declared category, and every required member of every category must be present at the expected artifact. A total-equality check would pass while one legitimate name vanished and one unexplained name appeared.

alias_prefixes.reason: A namespaced mirror of the committed corpus under the operator's reserved prefix, created when namespaces were introduced. Each name must resolve to the SAME artifact as the bare corpus name it mirrors; an alias that drifts is a hash mismatch, not an alias.

operational_probes.name: oath/step8-probe-disposable
operational_probes.reason: Created by an authority exercise validating delegated publication. Named after a step in a conversation, which is the naming mistake recorded in CLAUDE.md; the journal is append-only so documentation is the only correction available. Not standard library, not a definition anyone should depend on.

operational_probes.name: oath/step8-probe-second
operational_probes.reason: Second artifact of the same authority exercise, same defect in the same way.

registry_only.name: dbl
registry_only.reason: Journal sequence 1 — the registry's first entry, authored 'admin' on 2026-07-25. A bootstrap smoke test written directly against the store before the corpus was ever pushed. Kept because the journal is append-only; nothing depends on it.

registry_only.name: id-check
registry_only.reason: Written directly against the registry by the operator key on 2026-07-29 (journal 823, re-proven at 824). A manual check that never entered the committed corpus.

registry_only.name: transfer-example
registry_only.reason: A MISTAKE, recorded rather than tidied away. Intended as sandbox/transfer-example during the v0.10.0 transfer exercise; `oath publish` silently ignored an unknown --name flag and bound the definition's own bare name at the top level. Signed and owned, harmless, and permanently in the wrong place. The flag hole it exposed is fixed; the name cannot be.

legacy_unowned.derivation: A name is legacy-unowned iff its FIRST accepted journal binding is at or before boundary_seq AND carried no signature. DERIVED from immutable history, never stored — and closed by construction, since entries after the boundary are not eligible whatever they look like.
legacy_unowned.reason: Frozen 2026-08-01. These names are historically valid, owned only by an unverifiable label, protected operationally by policy.json, and superseded for real use by the owned michael/* mirrors. They are NOT adopted retroactively: a later signed republication proves authorship of that publication, not ownership of the original name.

demonstration_prefixes.reason: sandbox/* is a public namespace for protocol demonstrations, interoperability tests, and intentionally non-production artifacts. Names beneath it are expected and are NOT endorsement or standard-library membership. It exists so exercises have a correct permanent home instead of inventing throwaway names that turn out not to be throwaway.
